bullets.title: Fed's Waller Puts July Rate Hike On Table; Markets Price 45-50% Odds
bullets.body: Fed Governor Waller delivered the clearest hawkish signal yet, saying 'if there is another hot core reading on core inflation this week, U.S. policymakers should consider raising rates in the near term' and treating it as signal rather than noise. Markets repriced sharply: fed funds futures moved to 45-50% probability of a July hike (from 35% earlier), treasuries fell, and gold dropped 3%+ to ~$3,994/oz. Waller also floated a 1.5-2.5% inflation target band vs. the fixed 2% point, and dismissed reliance on forward guidance.

bullets.title: Oil +7% to $76/bbl on Hormuz Crisis; Iran Blockade Reinstated
bullets.body: Crude surged 7.3% above $76/bbl after Trump reinstated the Iranian blockade (with a 24-hour legal notification delay) and declared the U.S. 'Guardian of the Hormuz Strait,' proposing a 20% reimbursement fee on all cargo transiting the strait. Commercial crossings through Hormuz fell ~52% week-over-week (to just 3 transits), and Polymarket traders project crude above $80 this month. Saudi Arabia also intercepted two waves of Houthi ballistic missiles targeting a Saudi airbase, amplifying supply-risk premium.

bullets.title: Morgan Stanley Raises Hyperscaler Capex Forecasts to $1.2T (2027) / $1.4T (2028)
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley lifted its US hyperscaler capex estimates by 9-10%: $1.2 trillion by 2027 and $1.4 trillion by 2028. The bank explicitly dismissed the recent correction in AI infrastructure names as not signaling the end of the buildout. Separately, Big Tech (Google, Amazon, Microsoft, Meta, Oracle) has already accumulated nearly $700B in debt to fund AI data center spending.

bullets.title: TSMC June Revenue +67.9% YoY; Beats Q2 Guidance at $40.2B
bullets.body: TSMC reported June net revenue of NT$442.68B ($13.79B), up 67.9% year-over-year and 6.2% month-over-month, with H1 2026 revenue hitting $74.99B (+35.6% YoY). Q2 total revenue of $40.2B exceeded the high-end of guidance. Options market is pricing a 3.57% implied move around the earnings print scheduled for ~1:30am EDT on July 16.

bullets.title: Memory Supply Tight Until H2 2027; SK Hynix ADR Drops 9.9% on Profit-Taking
bullets.body: Semianalysis analyst Ray Wang says memory supply is unlikely to improve until H2 2027, with DRAM remaining constrained as chipmakers balance HBM demand from AI against commodity RAM. SK Hynix Korean shares fell a record 15.4% post-Nasdaq debut—analysts say the move reflects profit-taking and repricing between Korean shares and the US ADR, not weakening AI memory demand. SK Hynix ADR extended losses to session-low 9.9%.

bullets.title: MU: $233M Dark Pool Print; Long-Term Conviction Intact Despite Morning Selling
bullets.body: Micron continues to see an 'abnormal amount' of dark pool activity, with a fresh $233M print observed. A fintwit analyst noted memory/storage names (MU, SNDK) would get 'pulled down significantly' Monday morning alongside SK Hynix but maintained unchanged long-term conviction, flagging long-dated calendar spreads as an attractive way to play elevated volatility.

bullets.title: NVDA: Automotive Division Competing Internally for Compute; vLLM Performance Lead
bullets.body: Nvidia's head of automotive is fighting internally for compute allocation, reflecting extreme cross-divisional demand for Nvidia's resources. Separately, NVIDIA was praised for strong vLLM inference performance leadership while AMD was flagged as having 'a lot of catching up to do on certain models.' GTC Berlin conference early-bird pricing deadline is July 15.

bullets.title: META: $40B+ Louisiana Data Center; UBS Cuts PT to $766 from $865
bullets.body: Meta announced it will spend more than $40 billion on a Louisiana data center—one of the largest single data center commitments disclosed. Offsetting the bullish capex signal, UBS cut its META price target by ~11% to $766 from $865. A large block trade in META also hit the tape intraday, direction unclear.

bullets.title: INTC: €5B Ireland Fab 34 Investment for Xeon 6 / Diamond Rapids
bullets.body: Intel announced a €5 billion ($5.7B) investment at its Leixlip Fab 34 in Ireland to scale Intel 3 node production targeting Xeon 6 and next-gen Diamond Rapids processors, with capacity expansion targeted by 2027. Former Intel CEO Patrick Gelsinger, now a director, bought 153,846 shares for $500K (~$3.25/share) in coordinated insider buying alongside two other directors totaling $6M in a single day.

bullets.title: WBD: 12-State Lawsuit Filed to Block $110B Paramount Merger
bullets.body: California AG and 11 other states filed suit to block the Warner Bros. Discovery–Paramount merger, with California's AG presenting live. The deal, valued at $110 billion, now faces significant regulatory headwinds that could materially delay or derail the combination.

bullets.title: SPY A/D Line at All-Time Highs Despite Put Wall at 750
bullets.body: The SPY advance/decline line is hitting all-time highs, suggesting broad-based market strength despite bearish sentiment among some participants. However, gamma analysis shows SPY testing a $1.7-2B put wall at 750, with bulls needing to defend that level to avoid additional downside pressure.

bullets.title: Buffett Indicator Hits Record 234%; S&P Earnings Expected +24% YoY
bullets.body: The US stock market value-to-GDP ratio hit a new record of 234%, more than 3 standard deviations above its long-term historical average. Simultaneously, S&P 500 earnings are expected to increase 24% this year—a pace only seen outside post-recessionary rebounds—driven by outsized EPS gains in big tech.

bullets.title: Korean Market Stress: KOSPI 3rd Largest Drop Since Lehman; 1.2M Margin Calls
bullets.body: The KOSPI experienced its third-largest one-day drop since the Lehman crisis, with 1.2 million Korean leveraged retail accounts triggering margin calls as of July 13 and 320-360K accounts fully liquidated. Retail brokerage deposits fell 30 trillion won to their lowest since February 2020. Goldman's 1-Delta desk asked 'when does the KOSPI selling stop?'

bullets.title: Gold Falls 3%+ as Waller Hike Signal Overrides Iran Safe-Haven Bid
bullets.body: Spot gold dropped over 3% to ~$3,994/oz—down more than 20% from its January record high of $5,318/oz—as Fed Governor Waller's hawkish comments on near-term rate hikes outweighed the Middle East geopolitical risk premium. US 10-year yields moved to 4.60%, UK 10-year near 5%, German at 3.10%.

bullets.title: AI Capex Bond Issuance Testing Investor Limits; Banks Racing to Forecast $2T
bullets.body: A quarter-trillion-dollar wave of AI-related bond issuance is testing investor appetite as hyperscalers fund data center buildouts through debt markets. Multiple banks are now racing to be first to project $2 trillion in 2027 capex, though funding mechanisms at that scale remain unclear.

bullets.title: AAPL Sues OpenAI Over Stolen Secrets; Acquires SigScalr Assets
bullets.body: Apple filed a lawsuit against OpenAI alleging theft of trade secrets. Separately, Apple agreed to acquire certain assets and hire employees from SigScalr, a strategic move that received relatively less attention amid the broader market noise.

bullets.title: Semiconductor Wafer Growth Forecast Single Digits; Supply Deficit to Widen to 25% by 2030
bullets.body: Semiconductor wafer growth for both memory and logic is forecast to grow only single digits YoY. One analyst argues the market is 'super undersupplied even in 2030,' with the supply deficit projected to widen from 18% to 25% by 2030, while traditional cloud CPU volume grows only modestly (20M to 25M units) and physical AI gets near-zero allocation.

bullets.title: AVGO Market Cap Surpasses SpaceX at $1.9T vs $1.8T
bullets.body: Broadcom's market cap has grown back above SpaceX's as the latter fell to post-IPO lows (~$140, near its $135 IPO price), wiping approximately $1 trillion from SpaceX's peak valuation of $226/share. Broadcom currently stands at $1.9T market cap.

bullets.title: Software as AI Inverse Trade: UBER, SHOP Named as Holdings
bullets.body: One trader notes software stocks have been acting inversely to AI—rising when AI names fall and vice versa. UBER and SHOP were cited as specific holdings in a software-focused portfolio as the sector attempts to find a bottom.

bullets.title: Global Central Banks Reducing USD Exposure; Yen Weakens Past ¥162
bullets.body: Global central banks are reportedly planning to reduce US dollar exposure, signaling a strategic shift away from dollar reserves. Separately, the Japanese yen weakened past ¥162/USD after a media report suggested local pension funds would not face pressure to purchase more domestic securities, adding upward pressure on Japanese yields.
